goal.objective:
`src/index.js` holds a complete in-memory job scheduler, but its test suite fails. Find and fix the defects. Do not change the module's public surface, and do not change behaviour that the tests already accept: it must keep exporting `SchedulerError`, `ManualClock` and `Scheduler`, and every currently passing case must still pass. Editing the tests is not an option; they are restored before the checks run.

The intended behaviour is this. A job is submitted with an `id`, a `priority` (0 by default, higher runs first), a `runAtMs` release time (0), a `deadlineMs` (`Infinity`), a `durationMs` (1) and a list of `deps` that must already have been submitted. A submitted job is `pending`; from there it becomes `running`, then `done`, or it ends as `cancelled`, `missed` or `blocked`. A job is ready when it is pending, the clock has reached its release time, and every dependency has actually finished, so a dependency that is merely running does not release it. Among the ready jobs the scheduler starts the highest priority first, breaking ties by the earliest deadline and then by the smaller id, and it never runs more jobs at once than it has workers. Starting a job records the start time and schedules its completion at exactly `durationMs` later.

A job whose deadline has already passed when its turn to start arrives is `missed` rather than run; a job whose turn comes at exactly its deadline still runs. `cancel(id)` cancels a job that has not started yet and returns whether it did anything, so a running job, an already-cancelled job and a blocked job all answer false and are left alone. When a job is cancelled or missed, everything waiting on it can never run, so every pending job that depends on it becomes `blocked`, and so does every pending job that depends on those, all the way down. A job submitted when one of its dependencies has already failed is blocked immediately.

`tick()` moves the clock to the next moment at which anything can happen, completes the jobs whose time is up, then starts what fits, and returns false only when nothing is left to do; `runUntilIdle` ticks until then and returns the number of ticks. Every state change appends `{ at, type, id }` to the event log with the types `submit`, `start`, `complete`, `cancel`, `miss` and `block`, and the log, the job views and the report are copies that a caller cannot use to reach inside the scheduler. `ManualClock` never moves backwards, and invalid input throws `SchedulerError` with a `code`: `'BAD_JOB'`, `'DUPLICATE_JOB'`, `'UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY'`, `'UNKNOWN_JOB'`, `'BAD_OPTIONS'`, `'BAD_CLOCK'`, `'CLOCK_REGRESSION'` or `'TICK_LIMIT'`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.
